questions.q: Which action should be performed first on a compromised host?
options: Power it off to stop the attack
Reboot to get a clean state
questions.explain: RAM, processes, and connections are the most volatile evidence: rebooting or powering off destroys them.

questions.q: Match each artifact to its description.

pairs.right: Copy of RAM containing keys and processes
Quick point-in-time capture of a state
Timestamp, sender, size, and hash of data

questions.explain: These four artifacts have different scopes: memory, full disk, point-in-time state, and descriptive data.

questions.q: Which source reveals the exact payload of a network request?
questions.explain: NetFlow only describes the conversation; packet capture preserves the bytes exchanged.

questions.q: Which information must a chain of custody record? (Select all that apply)
options: The timestamp and source of collection
The collector's name and every transfer
questions.explain: Chain of custody tracks the identity and integrity of evidence, never authentication secrets.

questions.q: A legal hold is in effect. What must be done?
options: Delete data according to the 30-day policy
Share evidence with as many people as possible
questions.explain: A legal hold overrides the retention policy and requires preserving the relevant data.

questions.q: Two sources show conflicting timestamps. Which check is the priority?
options: Check NTP, time zone, and origin of the timestamps
questions.explain: A reliable timeline requires synchronized clocks: NTP, UTC, and time zones must be verified before interpretation.
